name: Vespid Dynamics Spore Cloud Disperser SCD-1 'Bloom'
description: A backpack-mounted dispersal system that releases clouds of engineered fungal spores designed to colonize and degrade specific material types. Different spore payloads target different substrates — one variant consumes synthetic polymers, another attacks ferrous metals, a third breaks down carbon-fiber composites. The spores germinate on contact with their target material and begin enzymatic degradation within hours, visibly consuming equipment, armor, vehicles, and infrastructure over a period of 2-5 days. Vespid developed the system for environmental remediation of industrial waste sites, but its application as a slow-acting area denial and equipment destruction weapon has not escaped military planners.
legality: Licensed — environmental remediation; Prohibited — all other use
specifications:
dispersal method: Backpack-mounted pressurized aerosol
cloud radius: 15-meter deployment zone per burst
spore germination: 2-6 hours on target substrate
full material degradation: 2-5 days depending on substrate
payload types: Polymer-consuming, ferrous metal-consuming, carbon composite-consuming
reservoir: 10 deployment bursts per tank
weight: 8 kg loaded
countermeasure: UV sterilization within 4 hours of exposure halts colonization
story_hooks: A Tier 3 armory's entire weapons stockpile was rendered useless overnight — polymer-consuming spores were introduced through the ventilation system, eating every synthetic component in the building.
Spore payloads designed to consume human-compatible biomedical polymers have been detected — if deployed, they would attack cybernetic implant housings inside living people.

physical_description.visual_profile: A biomechanical backpack system resembling a hybrid between military gear and laboratory equipment. The frame is angular and skeletal, with visible internal mechanisms and crystalline dispersal nozzles. Despite its destructive purpose, it has an almost organic aesthetic — segmented like an insect's abdomen, with a faint bioluminescent quality to its internal chambers.
physical_description.dimensions: 48 cm height × 35 cm width × 22 cm depth. Dual shoulder-mounted nozzles extend 12 cm forward from the frame. Central reservoir 30 cm tall.
physical_description.weight_description: Hefty and purposeful — 8 kg loaded feels substantial but balanced across the shoulders. The weight distribution centers low, designed for extended wear without fatigue.
physical_description.primary_material: Aircraft-grade aluminum frame with reinforced polycarbonate viewing ports. Internal plumbing combines titanium microtubes with biocompatible silicone valving. Nozzles are hardened ceramic-composite.
physical_description.finish: Matte gunmetal gray with translucent polymer sections revealing amber-tinted internal fluid. Sections show deliberate wear — scuffed corners, minor corrosion blooms on aluminum edges suggesting field use.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray primary, with amber and pale bioluminescent green accents. The spore solution inside glows faintly under dim light — a sickly organic luminescence.
physical_description.grip_texture: Rubberized shoulder harness with slight tackiness from fungal residue buildup. Control grips on chest-mounted trigger mechanism are textured polymer, slightly sticky to the touch.
distinctive_features: Dual crystalline dispersal nozzles with visible micro-jets
Transparent reservoir showing viscous amber liquid with suspended particulate matter
Segmented pressure relief vents along the spine — faintly glowing when charged
Organic growth patterns visible inside the polycarbonate — colonization marks from testing
Copper bioelectric contacts for spore type selection
Faint enzymatic smell — earthy, slightly chemical, vaguely unsettling
Pressure gauge with dual readout (reserve pressure / spore viability)
Heat-dispersal fins around the central chamber — warm to the touch when active
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: VESPID DYNAMICS logo embossed on left shoulder mount in chrome relief. Serial plate mounted on lower frame in small white text. Environmental certification stamps faded on rear — legitimate origin markers.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field-worn but maintained. The apparatus shows signs of regular use — minor fungal contamination marks on nozzle tips, slight discoloration on reservoir walls from repeated payloads, dust accumulated in pressure relief vents. This is a working tool, not a showpiece.
